LD 1774: An Act to Protect Domestic Workers - Testimony Neither For nor Against Bev Uhlenhake, on behalf of the Maine Association of Personal Care Agencies January 20, 2026
Senator Tipping, Representative Roeder, and distinguished members of the Labor Committee:
I appreciate the intent of the bill in consideration this afternoon. I appreciate Senator Talbot Ross' dedication to protecting workers, particularly those in fields which are primarily staffed by women and minorities. It is in the best interest of the State of Maine that these workers be protected.
I testify neither for nor against today because I believe there was a misstep in the bill's construction that will lead to unintended consequences for a workforce that is already struggling to hire, train, and retain employees.
Maine's licensed personal care agencies employ what could be considered "domestic workers" by this bill. Standards for these agency employees are already required to be met by these agencies through their licensing process, no matter if they are funded by the State through MaineCare or by other means. While the items laid out before you in this bill are generally not in conflict with PCA standards, I caution you against having two different standards in two different sections of Maine rules and laws that might be modified in the future in ways that are incongruent with one another.
With the above in mind, we recommend making the following amendment to �590. Definitions, 1. Domestic worker.
"Domestic worker" does not include an individual who is a family member; who is employed by a licensed personal care agency for the purpose of providing personal care in a client's residence, provides house sitting, pet sitting or dog walking services; or provides household repair or maintenance services.
Please note that there are personal care workers who are NOT protected through the licensing process (those hired through the self-directed care model within MaineCare). Therefore, an important group that should be protected by this bill would be missed if the carve out were to be for all personal care workers.
Thank you for your time and consideration in this matter. I'm happy to answer any questions you might have.
Respectfully submitted,
Bev Uhlenhake On behalf of the Maine Association of Personal Care Agencies

Re: LD 1774 - An Act to Protect Domestic Workers
Senator Tipping, Representative Roeder and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Labor:
Thank you for the opportunity to provide information for your consideration regarding LD 1774, An Act to Protect Domestic Workers.
LD 1774 would establish labor standards for domestic workers including requiring rules regulating the employment of domestic workers, requiring employers to engage in contracts for domestic employees, and implementing limitations on hours worked and rest breaks.
While the Department of Health and Human Services primarily defers to the Department of Labor on this bill, the Office of Child and Family Services (OCFS) is concerned with the proposed definition of "domestic worker." As written, the definition could be interpreted to include individuals who are employed by a licensed family child care provider that operates out of the provider's home (because they work in a residence and provide child care services). The inclusion of this group of employees does not appear to align with the intent of this bill.
If the Committee is inclined to move forward with this proposal, OCFS recommends adding language to the exception language in the definition of "domestic worker." The recommended language would be "or an individual employed to provide child care services in a child care program licensed under Title 22, Chapter 1673."
Please feel free to contact me if you have any questions during your deliberation of this bill.
Sincerely,

Bobbi L. Johnson, LMSW Director Office of Child and Family Services Maine Department of Health and Human Services
